topic: French society before the Revolution: the three estates, taxes and the subsistence crisis

Absence Note.Reason: I am attending a history teachers' workshop today.
Absence Note.Message to class: Keep your NCERT History book open at pages 4 and 5. Listen for who paid the taxes and why that made people angry.

Teaching Style.Tone: Calm storyteller; makes the past feel real with everyday comparisons
Teaching Style.Pace: Moderate; pauses after each cause to ask what it led to
Teaching Style.Language: Simple, clear English; explains each new word (estate, tithe, taille, subsistence) once in everyday words
Teaching Style.Habits: Starts with a question about fairness; asks the class to imagine being a peasant; links every cause to its effect

Lecture Structure.Order: France's empty treasury in 1774, the three estates with Fig. 2 from the book, who paid which taxes with Fig. 3 (The Spider and the Fly), the struggle to survive, how a subsistence crisis happens
Lecture Structure.Must cover: Fig. 2 from the book (the society of estates) and what it shows; Fig. 3 from the book (The Spider and the Fly) and why the noble is the spider and the peasant the fly; the three estates and that only the third estate paid taxes to the state; tithes, taille and indirect taxes; peasants were about 90 per cent of the population; population grew from 23 million to 28 million; the subsistence crisis as a chain of causes
Lecture Structure.Avoid: The storming of the Bastille and later events of the revolution; the middle class and the ideas of the philosophers (next class)

Next Class.Topic: A growing middle class and the ideas of Locke, Rousseau and Montesquieu
Next Class.Prep: Read pages 6 and 7 of the NCERT book

parts.title: The three estates: who was who (Fig. 2)
Peasants: about 90 per cent of the population, few owning land
Who paid which taxes: tithes, taille, indirect taxes and feudal dues
The struggle to survive: population growth and rising bread prices
